headline: A Thanksgiving storm brings 1.5 to 2 inches of rain (locally up to 3), damaging winds under a High Wind Warning for New York City and Long Island, and widespread moderate coastal flooding at both Thursday high tides, with the worst Thursday afternoon and evening.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday evening stays dry around New York City, with high pressure to the north and light east-northeast winds around 10 mph. Low clouds move into the city and Long Island's south shore around 1 AM Thursday, and winds ramp up through the night, reaching about 25 to 30 mph with gusts of 35 to 40 mph by the Thursday morning commute.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: The Thanksgiving storm remains on track, with the bulk of the rain and wind most likely Thursday afternoon and evening. A High Wind Warning runs from 10 AM Thursday to 1 AM Friday for New York City, Long Island and the Hudson, eastern Essex and eastern Union county areas of New Jersey, with gusts at the city airports of roughly 40 to 60 mph and possibly higher; a Wind Advisory from 10 AM Thursday to 5 AM Friday covers the rest of northeast New Jersey, Westchester, Rockland, southern Connecticut and now Orange and Putnam counties too. Moist air from the subtropics brings 1.5 to 2 inches of rain in general with local amounts up to 3 inches, heavy downpours at times and an isolated thunderstorm possible, especially toward Thursday evening. A dry slot ends the rain from southwest to northeast overnight, with winds turning southerly and easing, though some light rain or drizzle may linger; Friday brings scattered showers and a breezy southwest wind gusting roughly 30 to 40 mph.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday is mainly dry with west winds gusting about 25 to 30 mph, and Sunday looks quiet. A front on Monday brings a chance of showers with southwest gusts around 25 to 30 mph, turning northwest in the afternoon. The discussion gives no temperature details for these days.

coast: Gale- to storm-force east-northeast winds Thursday morning into Thursday night, on top of high tides after the recent full moon, make widespread moderate coastal flooding likely at both the Thursday morning and evening high tides, with potential for major flooding along the western Great South Bay and significant impacts around Peconic Bay and the Peconic River and along the western Long Island Sound shoreline; surge up the Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic rivers brings minor to moderate flooding. Thursday morning's tide is naturally higher by at least a foot, but the peak surge is expected Thursday afternoon and evening, so both tides may reach similar levels, and heavy rain during the evening tide could worsen coastal street flooding; forecasters leaned toward the higher-end water levels for a safety margin. Coastal Flood Warnings run 7 AM Thursday to 6 AM Friday for New York City, Long Island, northeast New Jersey's waterfront, southern Westchester and southwestern Connecticut (southern Middlesex and New London are under an advisory through 3 PM Friday). For Friday's morning tide, the earlier watch became an advisory for the north shore of Long Island, New York City (except southern Queens), northeast New Jersey, Westchester and southwestern Connecticut, where water should drain out and impacts be mainly minor, while a Coastal Flood Watch stays up for southern Queens, southern Nassau and southern Suffolk, where southwest winds could bring another round of moderate flooding, especially on the eastern Great South Bay. Ocean beaches see 8 to 12 foot breakers with widespread beach flooding, dune erosion and possible localized overwash; western Long Island Sound and the Twin Forks see 3 to 6 foot waves with dune erosion, splashover and possible isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures. On the water, a Gale Warning (6 PM Wednesday to 6 AM Thursday) gives way to a Storm Warning from 6 AM Thursday to 1 AM Friday, with ocean seas over 20 feet late Thursday afternoon and evening and waves near 10 feet on the Sound and the New York Harbor entrance; a southwest gale is likely on the ocean Friday, easing to small-craft-advisory levels Saturday and below that Sunday, with small-craft conditions possible again Monday.
watch_for: Timing of Thursday's strongest winds and rain could shift by 1 to 3 hours
Heavy downpours during Thursday evening's high tide worsening coastal street flooding
Friday morning's high tide on Long Island's south shore bays, still under a Coastal Flood Watch
confidence: Models are in good agreement on the Thursday storm, with only a few hours of timing uncertainty, and the coastal flood forecast deliberately leans toward the higher end; the weekend and Monday get little detail.
